body.heading: A blanket changes the meal
paragraphs: The food can be completely ordinary — sandwiches, fruit, cheese, leftovers. What makes it a picnic is the setting: a blanket on the floor, plates instead of the table, perhaps a jug of water with lemon in it because picnics have jugs. Children who pick at dinner will often eat happily off a blanket.

Shoes off, phones away, and if you want ceremony, an invitation. A paper note under each plate — 'you are invited to a picnic, bring a teddy' — costs nothing and changes the temperature of the whole meal.

body.heading: When it helps most
paragraphs: An indoor picnic is a good tool for evenings when everyone is tired and the normal routine feels heavy. It breaks the pattern without breaking the budget or the bedtime. Bad weather outside and a picnic inside is a combination children remember fondly.
It also works for a small celebration that does not need a party: the last day of term, a lost tooth, a Friday. Ordinary food, unusual place, a toast with water glasses.

body.heading: Clearing up, picnic rules
paragraphs: Everything goes back in one trip per person, picnic-basket style. The blanket gets shaken outside or over the bin, and the floor is restored in minutes — part of the charm is how little evidence remains.
If the picnic goes well, it can become the household's standard rescue for a long day: blanket, simple food, and a toast to whatever small thing deserves one.

description: Ordinary food on a blanket on the floor turns a tired weekday evening into a small occasion.
